--- title: "Where does the ballast go, and how much?" --- The neutral point from a straight-line fit of `Cm` against `CL` over α = 0–8° at 6 m/s, then the ballast mass that puts the CG a given static margin ahead of it. ::: {.callout-note} ## Assumed Static margin is not something the plan specifies, so three values are carried rather than one. The fit band is a choice too, not a measurement. ::: ::: {#6723ac66 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} mp0 = mass_properties() x_np = neutral_point(band=(0, 8), V=6.0) margins = [0.05, 0.10, 0.15] x_b = np.linspace(0, x_le_w, 200) m_b = {SM: ballast_for(x_np - SM * c_w, x_b, mp0) for SM in margins} nose = {SM: ballast_for(x_np - SM * c_w, 0.0, mp0) for SM in margins} le = {SM: ballast_for(x_np - SM * c_w, x_le_w, mp0) for SM in margins} DIME = 2.268e-3 # kg, a US dime, the plan's own ballast dime = mass_properties(m_ballast=DIME, x_ballast=0.0) ``` ::: **Answer.** On the nose, and about 3 g of it. Unballasted the airframe is unstable — 12\.52 g of foam puts the CG 184\.5 mm aft of the nose against a neutral point at 158\.0 mm, a static margin of \-30% MAC — because a stabilizer 35% the area of the wing, plus the fin, sit at the end of a 43\.8 cm fuselage. Station matters more than the mass does: 10% MAC costs 2\.98 g at the nose but 7\.99 g at the wing leading edge, where the plan says to tape the dime (@fig-ballast). A dime alone is not enough at this size; 2\.27 g on the nose lands the CG at 156\.2 mm, 1\.8 mm ahead of the neutral point, which is under half a percent of MAC and stable in name only. ::: {#tbl-ballast .cell tbl-cap='Ballast needed at each static margin, taped to the nose and taped at the wing leading edge, at 6 m/s.' execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import pandas as pd pd.DataFrame({ "static margin [% MAC]": [SM * 100 for SM in margins], "target CG [mm]": [(x_np - SM * c_w) * 1e3 for SM in margins], "on the nose [g]": [nose[SM] * 1e3 for SM in margins], "at the wing LE [g]": [le[SM] * 1e3 for SM in margins], }).style.format({ "static margin [% MAC]": "{:.0f}", "target CG [mm]": "{:.1f}", "on the nose [g]": "{:.2f}", "at the wing LE [g]": "{:.2f}", }).hide(axis="index") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ::: {#cell-fig-ballast .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4)) for SM in margins: ax.plot(x_b * 1e3, m_b[SM] * 1e3, label=f"static margin {SM:.0%} MAC") ax.axhline(DIME * 1e3, ls="--", c="0.4", lw=1, label=f"a dime, {DIME*1e3:.2f} g") ax.set_xlabel("ballast station [mm aft of the nose]") ax.set_ylabel("ballast mass [g]") ax.set_xlim(0, x_le_w * 1e3) ax.set_ylim(0, 15) ax.grid(alpha=0.3) ax.legend() plt.tight_layout() plt.show() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display} ![Ballast mass needed against the station it is taped to, from the nose back to the wing leading edge. The dashed line marks the 2.27 g of the dime the plan calls for.](2026-08-27-02-where-does-the-ballast-go-and-how-much_files/figure-html/fig-ballast-output-1.png){#fig-ballast width=1036 height=585} ::: ::: ::: {.callout-note collapse="true"} ## The method, as called ```python def neutral_point(airplane=None, band=(0.0, 8.0), V=6.0): """ Neutral point [m aft of the nose], from a straight-line fit of Cm vs CL. The moment reference is read off the airplane rather than passed in. AeroBuildup reports Cm about `xyz_ref`, and the answer is only meaningful measured from that same station; sourcing the two separately silently biases the result by the offset between them. That error once doubled a reported sensitivity before it was caught. This is one of the few places worth NOT using the library's own function. `run_with_stability_derivatives()` returns x_np from the identical formula, but by finite-differencing at a point; at this Reynolds number Cm against CL is genuinely curved, so that answer moves with the angle you take it at -- 147 to 197 mm across the same band. This returns the average slope over a stated range instead. Neither removes the choice, so `band` is an explicit argument every entry declares. """ ap = mceagle if airplane is None else airplane p = polars(ALPHA_SWEEP, V=V, airplane=ap) CL, Cm = np.array(p["CL"]), np.array(p["Cm"]) k = (ALPHA_SWEEP >= band[0]) & (ALPHA_SWEEP <= band[1]) return ap.xyz_ref[0] - np.polyfit(CL[k], Cm[k], 1)[0] * c_w def ballast_for(x_cg_target, x_ballast=0.0, mp=None): """ Point mass [kg] at `x_ballast` that moves the CG to `x_cg_target`. The CG of structure plus ballast is a mass-weighted mean, so the mass needed follows from the lever ratio. Defaults to the unballasted airframe. """ m = mass_properties() if mp is None else mp return m.mass * (m.x_cg - x_cg_target) / (x_cg_target - x_ballast) ``` :::
